Heatmap of a quantitative matrix, clustered or in annotation order

Source: R/plots.R
plot_quant_heatmap.Rd

ggplot2 tile heatmap of the most variable features, drawn either with hierarchical clustering of both dimensions (cluster = TRUE) or in the order given by the annotation table (cluster = FALSE) — the two views answer different questions: whether the data cluster by condition on their own, and how the conditions look side by side as designed. Unlike plot_heatmap(), which writes a png through gplots::heatmap.2, this returns a ggplot object that can be printed inside a knitted tabset.

Usage

plot_quant_heatmap(
  mat,
  coldata,
  cluster = TRUE,
  top_n = 500,
  center_rows = TRUE,
  title = NULL
)

Arguments

mat

Numeric matrix of log2 intensities.

coldata

Matching column metadata (Unit, Condition).

cluster

Cluster rows and columns (TRUE, default) or keep the annotation order (FALSE).

top_n

Number of most variable features to show. Default 500.

center_rows

Subtract the feature mean, so the colour encodes the log2 ratio to the feature average rather than absolute abundance. Default TRUE.

title

Plot title. Default NULL (auto-generated).

Value

A ggplot object, or NULL (with a warning) when the matrix is empty.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot_quant_heatmap(mat_n, qm$coldata, cluster = TRUE, top_n = 300)
} # }
